definitions.gloss: amber color; caramel color; honey color
definitions.explanation: A translucent golden-brown color resembling that of traditional Japanese hard candy. Commonly used to describe slowly caramelized onions, varnished wood, or aged objects.

examples.japanese: {玉|たま}ねぎを{飴色|あめいろ}になるまで{炒|いた}める。
examples.english: Fry the onions until they turn caramel-colored.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{家具|かぐ}が{飴色|あめいろ}に{輝|かがや}いていた。
examples.english: The old furniture glowed an amber color.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}の{使|つか}い{込|こ}んだ{机|つくえ}は{長年|ながねん}の{使用|しよう}で{美|うつく}しい{飴色|あめいろ}になっていた。
examples.english: My grandfather's well-used desk had taken on a beautiful amber color from years of use.

notes:
Composed of {飴|あめ} (candy) + {色|いろ} (color). Often signals warmth, age, and quality — used positively for both cooked foods and well-aged wooden objects.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {飴色|あめいろ}の{玉|たま}ねぎ: caramelized onions
- {飴色|あめいろ}になるまで{炒|いた}める: to fry until caramel-colored
- {飴色|あめいろ}の{家具|かぐ}: amber-colored furniture

SIMILAR WORDS:
- きつね{色|いろ}: golden brown — describes the color of well-fried food (toast, tempura, fried chicken); lighter than {飴色|あめいろ}
- {琥珀色|こはくいろ}: amber color — more formal/literary; often used for whiskey, tea, and gemstones
